title: documents filed from a mail attachment are visible to whoever may read the mail
detail: The `inbound-message` read model now declares `access.read` for the member roles: shared mailboxes are readable by every member, a personal mailbox only by its owner, admins included. `createInboundMessageEntity(memberRoles)` builds the entity for the configured roles; `inboundMessageEntity` stays exported with the default roles. The message queries filter rows as before and do not use this rule.

title: Inbound HTML sanitizer keeps quote markers so the reader can fold quoted text
detail: The sanitizer stripped class and type attributes, so the reader never found the quote of Gmail, Apple Mail, Thunderbird, Yahoo or Outlook mails. It now keeps blockquote type="cite", the classes gmail_quote, moz-cite-prefix and yahoo_quoted on div and blockquote, and the ids appendonsend and divRplyFwdMsg on div; every other class, id and type is still removed. The reader's HTML quote detection also folds moz-cite-prefix and yahoo_quoted.

title: Sanitized HTML body on inbound messages (message.bodyHtml, event version 4)
detail: ingest-message and attach-message-content run the HTML part of a mail through sanitizeInboundHtml (sanitize-html allowlist for tags, attributes, schemes and style properties; no scripts, forms, on* attributes, cid: or data: images; img src only absolute http(s), a href only absolute http(s), mailto or tel, so nothing resolves against the app origin; links open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer"; empty or over 500,000 bytes of UTF-8 becomes null instead of a cut-off body). Only the sanitized result reaches the event and the projection, PII-encrypted for the tenant like bodyText; the unsanitized original stays in file storage. inbound-message-received and inbound-message-content-fetched are version 4 with bodyHtml (older events upcast to null), the entity message has the new field bodyHtml, and message:content returns bodyHtml (string or null); the message list leaves bodyHtml out like bodyText.
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate <name>` in each app that mounts inbound-mail-foundation to get the migration for the new column read_inbound_messages.body_html. Existing messages keep bodyHtml null and show their plain text; nothing else to do.

title: The inbound mail supervisor requires a lock and the dedup anchor is unique
detail: `createInboundMailSupervisor` takes a required `lock` (a DistributedLock) instead of an optional one, so only one worker holds the IMAP watch per account; the single-process path without a lock is gone. The unmanaged table store_mail_seen_messages gets a unique index on (account_id, provider_message_id), which the ingest comment always promised; ingest-message already serialized concurrent ingests of one mail with a per-message advisory lock, so the second one reports duplicate.
migration: Pass `lock: createDistributedLock(redis, "kumiko:lock:inbound-mail:watch:")` to createInboundMailSupervisor. Run `kumiko-schema generate <name>` in each app that mounts inbound-mail-foundation to get the migration for the unique index on store_mail_seen_messages; existing rows must hold no duplicate (account_id, provider_message_id).

title: Imported mails store full text, original and attachments
detail: ingest-message now takes bodyText (at most 32,000 characters, cut with bodyTextTruncated set; 32,000 keeps a long mail readable while one event, one projection row and the PII-encrypted column stay small, the original keeps everything), rawMime, bodyHtml, attachments (at most 50) and skippedAttachments (at most 200). The original is stored as .eml (or .html for HTML-only mails) and each attachment as a file reference through file storage; apps without a file provider still import the mail, mark contentState unavailable and show the mailbox as interrupted. The event inbound-message-received is now v2 with an upcast that defaults the new fields; bodyText is personal tenant data. The new query inbound-mail-foundation:query:message:content returns text, original reference and attachments of one mail; message:list never carries the body. Retention removes the mail row, its body object and its attachment files. RawInboundMessage gains text, html, attachments and skippedAttachments.

title: A mail that cannot be parsed is quarantined instead of blocking the mailbox
detail: A mail the provider reports as rejected, or whose ingest fails, is normalized where possible and otherwise stored in the unmanaged table store_mail_quarantine; every message is isolated in the supervisor, so the rest of the batch imports and the sync cursor moves on. An ingest failure only counts against a mail once a later mail of the batch succeeded, and the third counted failure quarantines it as ingest_failed; an outage of the database, KMS or file storage never quarantines good mail and never moves the cursor past an unhandled mail. The account list shows quarantinedCount and lastError, the new handler acknowledge-quarantine confirms the entries, acknowledged entries are purged by retention after 90 days, and the tenant-destroy hook removes them.

title: A mailbox that stops syncing shows as interrupted with a reason
detail: The account events mail-account-connected and mail-account-updated are v2 with lastError (connection_failed, rate_limited, message_quarantined, file_storage_unavailable). Three failed polls in a row set the status degraded, shown as Unterbrochen in German; the next successful poll sets it back to active. New key in all locale packages.

title: A disconnected mailbox is reactivated under the same account
detail: The new handler reactivate-account puts a disconnected mailbox back to active with its stream and sync cursor, so no mail is imported twice. connect-account refuses an address that is already connected (address_already_connected) or disconnected (address_disconnected) and reopens a disconnected OAuth mailbox in place; connect-routes answers 409 with the reason. reconnect-mailbox now also accepts a disconnected account.

title: Snippet-only mails get their content reloaded
detail: Mails imported before this change carry only a snippet. The supervisor asks the provider for their content through fetchContent and stores it with attach-message-content (event inbound-message-content-fetched v1); a mail the server no longer has becomes unavailable and is not asked for again.

title: Connected, reconnected and reactivated mailboxes sync immediately
detail: A per-instance event consumer wakes the supervisor on a new or active-again mailbox, which syncs once right away instead of waiting for the next poll. A sync of one account never runs twice at the same time. A woken sync that finds the credential not stored yet (the OAuth secret is written after the account) sets no status and leaves it to the next tick; stop() waits for running syncs.

title: The first sync after an OAuth connect no longer waits for the next poll
detail: The OAuth callback now dispatches the internal handler mark-credential-stored once the refresh token is saved, so the sync that the account commit triggers earlier than the token is repeated as soon as the credential exists. Originals above 50 MB are not stored; they are listed in skippedAttachments as message/rfc822 with reason too_large while text and attachments are kept. attach-message-content no longer accepts a caller-supplied bodyRef.

title: Outgoing mail carries attachments
detail: sendMailFromAccount takes attachmentFileIds (at most 10 file references of the caller's tenant, at most 18 MB together, duplicates dropped). The bytes are read through file storage and sent over SMTP and stored in the sent folder unchanged; an unknown or foreign file gives mail_send_attachment_invalid, too many bytes mail_send_attachments_too_large, and nothing is sent. The plugin method send now receives the resolved attachments as a fourth argument and returns ProviderSentMail. New keys in all locale packages.

title: A hanging mailbox no longer blocks the others
detail: The supervisor syncs up to 4 accounts at the same time (pollConcurrency), skips an account whose previous sync is still running, and abandons a sync after 10 minutes (accountPollDeadlineMs) as one failed poll; plugin.fetch and plugin.fetchContent receive an AbortSignal, and an abandoned sync stores nothing and moves no cursor. The IMAP client sets connection (20 s) and greeting (16 s) timeouts explicitly.

title: Sender authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) of imported mails
detail: inbound-message-received v2 carries senderAuthentication ({ authservId, spf, dkim, dkimDomains, dmarc, fromDomain } or null; verdicts pass, fail, none, unknown; dkimDomains at most 10), stored as JSON text in read_inbound_messages.sender_authentication and returned by message:content and loadInboundMessageContent; isSenderAuthenticated is true only for a dmarc pass. The mail account has a new optional trustedAuthservId (events mail-account-* v2, read_mail_accounts.trusted_authserv_id, input of connect-account, update-account, reactivate-account and the IMAP connect and reconnect forms). Only the first Authentication-Results header from the top whose authserv-id equals it counts; without an id, without such a header or when its header.from domain differs from the From domain the result is null, and a dmarc result without header.from is unknown. Headers below the trusted one are ignored, so a sender cannot inject a pass. Mails imported before, and content refetched later, have null. New keys in all locale packages.

title: Mail account handlers are stricter and the trusted authserv-id has its own handler
detail: trustedAuthservId is no longer accepted by connect-account, update-account and reactivate-account (strict schemas reject unknown keys); set it with the new set-trusted-authserv-id (SystemAdmin, TenantAdmin, not model-callable). update-account accepts status, lastError, watchState and reason only from the system identity; connect-account is no longer exposed to agents. reactivate-account checks the account owner (unless the OAuth override is set), fails with credential_required when a password account has no stored credential, and reopens an account in place only with that override; disconnect-account deletes the stored secret. Outgoing attachments must pass the file read check of the sender, and SendMailFromAccountContext needs dispatch. New screen "Absenderprüfung" edits the id. The watch supervisor and the IMAP forms use mapWithConcurrency and implicit TLS on port 465 for SMTPS.
migration: Drop trustedAuthservId from connect-account, update-account and reactivate-account payloads and dispatch set-trusted-authserv-id after connecting. Wrapping or agent setups that called connect-account as a model tool need their own exposed handler. Callers of sendMailFromAccount pass a context that includes dispatch. Personal mailboxes are reactivated by their owner only; after disconnect-account a new credential must be stored before reactivate-account.

title: The mailbox row action Reconnect is folded into Reactivate
detail: The row action reconnect of mailAccountListScreen and its i18n key inboundMail.accounts.reconnect are removed. A password IMAP mailbox with a sign-in error now shows Reactivate, which opens the same screen mail-account-reconnect-imap; OAuth mailboxes get the client action reactivate-oauth instead.
migration: Apps that override inboundMail.accounts.reconnect move the text to inboundMail.accounts.reactivate. Apps that reference the row action id reconnect (tests, screen extensions) use reactivate for password IMAP and reactivate-oauth for OAuth mailboxes, and mount inboundMailFoundationClient() from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/inbound-mail-foundation/web so the OAuth action runs.

title: The OAuth callback only connects a personal mailbox for the account that signed in
detail: InboundOAuthFlow.exchangeCode returns OAuthCodeExchange, an OAuthTokenSet with the required accountAddress of the signed-in provider account. The callback compares it with the mailbox address, ignoring case, and answers 403 mailbox_address_mismatch with a plain-text message and no account when they differ, so nobody can claim another person's address. This applies to personal mailboxes; a shared mailbox (only admins start that flow) is often opened with the admin's own login through delegated access, as with M365 shared mailboxes, so its address is not compared, and a token without access to it shows auth_error on the first sync.
migration: Inbound providers with an oauth block return accountAddress from exchangeCode, taken from the token's email claim or the provider's profile endpoint (for example the userinfo email). There is no default: a provider that cannot name the signed-in address cannot connect mailboxes.

title: Failing ingests are counted and a poison mail is quarantined after three intervals
detail: The supervisor counts an ingest failure once per poll interval in the unmanaged table store_mail_ingest_failures, but only when another mail of the account went through in the same poll (for a storage failure another storage write); at three it quarantines the mail with reason ingest_failed and moves the cursor on, before that the batch stops and nothing behind it is skipped. A failure nothing proves to be the mail's (KMS, file storage, the app's storeBody hook, the ingest handler or projection failing for every mail) counts nothing (when every failure of a poll was counted before as a storage or ingest failure, they all keep counting), keeps the cursor and sets the account to degraded with lastError encryption_unavailable, file_storage_unavailable or ingest_unavailable; the next interval retries. An account the supervisor cannot poll because the key store fails while decrypting its address is set to encryption_unavailable too, instead of being skipped silently. A mail that waits for its count clears a shown encryption_unavailable or ingest_unavailable, and file_storage_unavailable once a storage write went through. A requested quarantine retry also runs while a failing mail holds the cursor; during an outage, and when a reload fails because of the provider, the KMS or file storage, the request stays and runs after the recovery. Every quarantined mail also gets a header-only entry (contentState unavailable, contentUnavailableReason quarantined); after a storage failure it goes without the original.

title: Quarantined mails can be retried
detail: The write handler retry-quarantined-message (mailbox owner or admin) flags a quarantine entry; the next successful sync loads the mail again, attaches the content to the header entry or ingests it in full, and removes the entry.

title: inbound-message-received is v3 and inbound-message-content-fetched is v2
detail: Both events carry contentUnavailableReason (null for older events through upcasters). The read table read_inbound_messages gets content_unavailable_reason, store_mail_quarantine gets retry_requested_at, and store_mail_ingest_failures is new; generate and apply a migration with `kumiko-schema generate`. ingest-message and attach-message-content upload files before their transaction when called at top level, and attach-message-content skips the upload when the mail already shows its content; inside a wrapper handler's transaction they upload in it, as before. RejectedInboundMessage may carry rawMime and headers, and an inbound provider's fetch may take filterUnknownMessageIds to skip mails that are already known.
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` and apply the migration; read_inbound_messages is rebuilt from events because attachment_file_ids becomes jsonb. Consumers that read the event payloads type them against the new versions (upcasters fill contentUnavailableReason with null). To get the pre-transaction upload, trigger on inbound-message-received or inbound-message-content-fetched instead of wrapping ingest-message in an own write handler.

title: A watch that starts during a sync catches up on mail that arrived before it opened
detail: After a successful watch start the supervisor runs one catch-up poll (after a running sync finished), and a tick also starts the watch while the account is still syncing. Mail delivered between the last poll and the watch opening is imported without waiting for the poll interval. The watch start is idempotent per account.

title: Exports for consumers of content events and attachment names
detail: INBOUND_MESSAGE_CONTENT_FETCHED_EVENT_QN, its payload type and schema, and readableFileName({ id, fileName }) are exported from the feature index, so an app can react to fetched content and show decrypted attachment names.

title: Reactivate a disconnected mailbox from the mailbox list
detail: list-accounts returns reactivateVia per mailbox (password_form, oauth_flow or null) for a disconnected mailbox or one with a sign-in error, set only for the owner of a personal mailbox and for admins of a shared one. The mailbox list shows Reactivate for password_form; the new dormant screen my-mail-accounts (MY_MAIL_ACCOUNT_LIST_SCREEN_ID, role User) and the admin list show Reactivate for oauth_flow as the client action inbound-mail-foundation:reconnect-oauth, which goes through GET /api/inbound-mail/connect and the callback again and reopens the mailbox under its old id; apps mount it with inboundMailFoundationClient() from inbound-mail-foundation/web. The callback also reopens an OAuth mailbox with a sign-in error. It switches a reopened mailbox back on only after the new refresh token is stored; when storing fails it answers 502 credential_store_failed with a plain-text message and the mailbox keeps its previous state. reactivate-account admits the system user for this step. reactivate-account admits role User, gated by the owner rule for personal mailboxes, and requires a credential for disconnected, auth_error and degraded alike. set-trusted-authserv-id is a tenant security policy: only SystemAdmin and TenantAdmin change it, on every mailbox of the tenant including personal ones. The connect route answers 403 shared_mailbox_requires_admin when a user without admin role starts the shared flow. The row action Reconnect is folded into Reactivate (see the breaking entry). The connect-mailbox form reopens a disconnected shared IMAP mailbox of the same address under its old account id with the new password. For anything else connect-account answers with a text pointing to Reactivate, and credential_required from reactivate-account is a plain-text message. A new i18n key set (de, en, fr, es, it) is part of the locale packages.

title: Quarantined mails are listed with sender and subject and handled one by one
detail: The query quarantine:list and the dormant screen mail-quarantine show the open entries of the mailboxes the caller may manage, with sender and subject from the header-only import (empty without one), reason and date; row actions fetch a mail again or confirm it. acknowledge-quarantine takes an optional providerMessageId (without it all entries of the mailbox as before) and now also admits the owner of a personal mailbox (role User). The mailbox list gets a row action Quarantine for mailboxes with open entries.

title: Mail attachments are bound to the mail and follow its visibility
detail: The attachment fileRefs of an imported mail are bound to the inbound-message record (field attachmentFileIds). GET /files/:id answers with the mail's visibility: owner and admins for a personal mailbox, whoever may see the mail for a shared one. The new query inbound-message:detail ({ id }) backs that check and is not exposed to agents. Outbound attachments use the same rule (canCallerReadFileRef). Retention now also removes the attachment files of a purged mail. read_inbound_messages.attachment_file_ids is jsonb; the migration 0056 carries a table rebuild marker, so the read table is rebuilt from the events. InboundMessageContent.attachmentFileIds stays string[].

title: Personal mail is private to its owner, roles are configurable
detail: Admins no longer read messages, bodies, attachments or quarantine of a personal mailbox; list-accounts still shows them the account without counts. The screens and the IMAP handlers are factories (createMailAccountListScreen, createImapConnectScreen and others) taking the resolved roles instead of constants. The content-fetched event is version 3 with accountId and ownerUserId. createDefaultGuard has a fourth parameter recordOnlyEntityTypes; for those entity types the files privilegedRoles no longer read or delete attached files (shared mailboxes included), only the uploader and readers of the record do. The OAuth connect route answers 403 mail_role_required to callers without a mail role.
migration: Apps that import mailAccountListScreen, mailAccountEditScreen, mailAccountSenderCheckScreen, myMailAccountListScreen, mailQuarantineScreen, imapConnectScreen or imapReconnectScreen call the matching create*Screen factory with resolveInboundMailRoles(). Apps with their own roles pass { userRoles, adminRoles } to createInboundMailFoundationFeature and the same options to createInboundProviderImapFeature. Callers of createDefaultGuard pass a Set of record-only entity types as fourth argument. Code that read personal mail as an admin must run as the owner; the nullable accountId and ownerUserId on content-fetched events need no action.

title: Supervisor and OAuth callback writes work when the app roles leave out SystemAdmin
detail: `update-account`, `connect-account` and `reactivate-account` are dispatched as the system user by the watch supervisor, the account health and the OAuth callback, but their access list held only the configured `adminRoles`/`memberRoles`. An app whose roles exclude SystemAdmin saw every health, watch-state and callback write refused ("health update was rejected"), so mailboxes never showed `degraded`. These three handlers now also accept SystemAdmin (the list is `SYSTEM_DISPATCHED_MAIL_HANDLERS`). `isMailAdmin`, screens and what real users may do stay on the configured roles.

title: The mail account list offers Reconnect for accounts with a sign-in error
detail: A new row action Reconnect opens the screen mail-account-reconnect-imap of inbound-provider-imap. It shows for every account with status auth_error and, like the Connect mailbox button, only renders in apps that mount that provider. New export IMAP_RECONNECT_SCREEN_ID. New key in all locale packages.

title: Mailbox names are stored without surrounding spaces
detail: connect-account and update-account trim displayName before storing it, so a name pasted with a leading space no longer shows and sorts with it. connect-account still accepts an empty name as before.

title: Mail sync no longer fails when reading IMAP credentials
detail: createInboundMailSupervisor builds its provider context with auditUserId defaulting to the system user. Apps that did not set auditUserId in providerCtx got an internal error on every fetch and watch because the secrets context needs an audit identity. An explicitly set auditUserId is kept.

title: Mail sync finds the stored IMAP credentials under row-level security
detail: createInboundMailSupervisor runs outside any request, so secret reads ran without a tenant scope and the application role saw no row in read_tenant_secrets. The supervisor now wraps providerCtx.secrets with tenantScopedSecrets, which the framework exports from internal/row-level-security. inbound-provider-inmemory gains requireCredentialSecretOnFetch so tests can exercise credential reads; a new integration test runs the secrets against an application-role database.

title: Mail polling works with the row-level-security enforcing pool
detail: createInboundMailSupervisor opens its own system scope for the cross-tenant reads and writes of accounts, cursors and seen messages. Before, passing the enforcing pool as db made every poll see no accounts.

title: The mail account list links to the IMAP connect form
detail: mailAccountListScreen gets a "Connect mailbox" toolbar action that opens the screen mail-account-connect-imap. The button shows only when the app mounts inbound-provider-imap, which registers that screen. The Systemcheck fix link for inbound mail now leads to a list where a mailbox can be added.

title: Apps can send from a connected mailbox
detail: The provider contract gets an optional send(ctx, account, message). The new server function sendMailFromAccount(ctx, { accountId, message }) is called from an app's own write handler and sends through the provider of the mailbox, with the mailbox address as From and In-Reply-To and References for replies. It returns WriteResult<{ messageIdHeader }>; failures are typed UnprocessableErrors with the reasons mail_send_not_configured, mail_send_login_rejected, mail_send_server_unreachable, mail_send_rejected and mail_send_invalid_message (i18n keys inboundMail.send.errors.*). A missing, disconnected or someone else's personal mailbox answers not found. There is no fallback to the app sender. New exports: sendMailFromAccount, MAIL_SEND_ERRORS, outboundMailMessageSchema, OutboundMailMessage, OutboundMailSent, MailSendNotConfiguredError, MailSendRejectedError. New keys in all locale packages.

title: Inbound-mailbox probes
detail: inbound-mail-foundation registers a probe with one result per configured mailbox. A personal mailbox is probed only when its owner starts the run, and only its owner sees the result.

title: Undecryptable mail account no longer stops polling of other accounts
detail: Any decryption failure of an account address (corrupt envelope, missing key, AAD mismatch) is logged by error class and the account is skipped; the other accounts keep polling.

title: Rename audit reason comes from the caller role
detail: update-account records tenant_admin or system_admin from the caller's roles and honors a client-supplied reason only for the system identity, so a form call can no longer write system reasons such as watch_supervisor. The rename form no longer carries a reason field and the reason payload field is optional.

title: Seen-message lookup handles listings of any size
detail: filterUnknownMessageIds queries the already seen provider message ids in chunks of 1000, so a full-mailbox listing no longer exceeds the Postgres bind parameter limit and aborts the account's poll.

title: Mailbox list accepts the screen's limit
detail: account:list accepted an empty payload only, so the projectionList screen's limit was rejected. It now takes limit up to MAX_LIST_LIMIT and returns the visible mailboxes ordered by id.

title: Declarative mailbox list and rename screens
detail: The feature registers the projectionList mail-accounts (name, address, provider, status, connected; row actions rename and disconnect) and the actionForm mail-account-edit, both restricted to SystemAdmin and TenantAdmin like the handlers. The list shows several mailboxes per tenant, never a credential. Screens are dormant, so the app places the list in its own nav. MAIL_ACCOUNT_LIST_SCREEN_ID and MAIL_ACCOUNT_EDIT_SCREEN_ID are exported.
migration: Place mail-accounts in the app nav with r.nav; no other change.

title: The deprecated inboundMailFoundationFeature constant is removed
detail: inboundMailFoundationFeature was kept next to createInboundMailFoundationFeature() for one release. Mount the feature by calling createInboundMailFoundationFeature().
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It replaces inboundMailFoundationFeature with createInboundMailFoundationFeature().

title: Inbound mail fetch can skip already-seen message ids
detail: InboundMailProviderPlugin.fetch receives an optional filterUnknownMessageIds(providerMessageIds) hook. The watch supervisor implements it with a tenant- and account-scoped lookup of already-seen provider message ids and returns the ids not seen yet, so a plugin can avoid downloading messages it has already processed.

title: InboundMailContext exposes metricsFor to provider plugins
detail: InboundMailContext gains an optional metricsFor(featureName) returning a MetricsHandle. runProdApp, the worker app and the dev server wire it from the observability meter, so provider plugins can emit their own metrics through the same pipeline.
migration: Code that builds SystemWireDeps itself adds metricsFor (createMetricsForFactory(meter)).

title: Watch supervisor skips and logs accounts whose address does not decrypt
detail: Previously a single such account made the whole account snapshot throw.

title: Inbound mail projections use typed bun-db helpers
detail: Mail-account and mail-thread events upsert through `upsertOnConflict` (`connectedAt` is only written on insert), inbound messages insert through `insertOnConflictDoNothing`. The raw `db/queries/inbound-projections.ts` module is gone.

title: Inbound mail OAuth accounts refresh their access token
detail: `createInboundMailSupervisor` obtains a valid access token via the new `createOAuthAccessTokenManager` before `plugin.fetch`/`plugin.watch` for accounts whose provider declares `oauth` and whose authMethod is `oauth`/`xoauth2`, and passes it as `opts.accessToken` (`fetch`) or `{ accessToken }` (`watch`, 4th argument). `refreshAccessToken` receives an optional 4th argument `{ signal }` (aborted after 30 s); providers must pass it to their token-endpoint fetch, since the foundation awaits the provider and never drops a late result. The foundation has no single construction point for routes and supervisor, so apps that want connect to prime the cache and write under the refresh lock create one manager with `createOAuthAccessTokenManager({ db, secrets })` and pass it to both `createInboundMailSupervisor({ oauthTokens })` and `createInboundMailConnectRoutes({ oauthTokens })`; without it the supervisor builds its own manager and the callback writes the secret without the lock. `InboundAuthError` from `refreshAccessToken` moves the account to `auth_error`; the generic sync-error log and the `token_exchange_failed` response body no longer contain provider error messages.
migration: Apps with OAuth inbound accounts create one `createOAuthAccessTokenManager({ db, secrets })` and pass it as `oauthTokens` to both `createInboundMailSupervisor` and `createInboundMailConnectRoutes`. Provider plugins with a `refreshAccessToken` pass the `signal` from its fourth argument to their token-endpoint fetch.

title: Poll cursor is persisted with the account's tenantId
detail: Several bundled-feature fixes. The inbound-mail watch supervisor now stamps `tenantId` when it first saves a poll cursor, so cursors persist instead of failing on the NOT NULL column. The anonymous queries of managed-pages, template-resolver, seo, compliance-profiles and auth-email-password rate-limit per IP and handler, so one handler no longer drains the bucket of the others. The personal-access-token list loads up to the maximum page size without a pager that could not page. Serial host ids beyond int4 are denied as not found, and the notes forget hook resolves the tenant retention preset once.

title: OAuth callback fails before creating an account when no secrets context is wired
detail: The inbound-mail OAuth callback now checks for a configured secrets context before exchanging the authorization code and creating the mail account. Without secrets the callback answers 500 `secrets_context_missing` and no orphan account is left behind. `form-draft:get` now logs a warning when a stored draft blob fails its schema instead of dropping it silently.

title: Tenant destroy no longer fails on mail-account, inbound-message and mail-thread rows
detail: The inbound-mail tenant-destroy hooks passed the tenant-scoped TenantDb they receive into raw DbRunner helpers, so the app-data stage failed and the tenant ended in destroyFailed. They now use ctx.db methods and declare an escapeHatch for the event-stream archive.

title: createInboundMailConnectRoutes() returns ExtraRouteDefinition[] with static options only
migration: createInboundMailConnectRoutes(options) now returns readonly ExtraRouteDefinition[] (connect route as entry: "user", callback route as entry: "signature") instead of mounting itself on app. options is now static config only - any db/registry/dispatch values previously passed through options are supplied by the framework via the route's deps instead. Replace extraRoutes: (app, deps) => createInboundMailConnectRoutes(options)(app, deps) with extraRoutes: createInboundMailConnectRoutes(options) (spread into the app's route array alongside other route definitions).

title: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine` bekommt `ctx.tryAppendEvent` — ein savepoint-scope…
detail: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine` bekommt `ctx.tryAppendEvent` — ein savepoint-scoped Gegenstück zu `ctx.unsafeAppendEvent`, das `VersionConflictError` als `{ ok: false, conflict }` zurückgibt statt zu werfen, ohne die restliche Handler-Transaktion zu poisonen (Bun.SQL/ postgres.js brechen den gesamten `begin()` bei einem ungefangenen Statement- Fehler ab, SQLSTATE 25P02, selbst wenn der JS-Error gefangen wird — `tryAppendEvent` läuft dafür in einem echten `SAVEPOINT`). `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/inbound-mail-foundation`: der `ingest-message`-Handler nutzt `ctx.tryAppendEvent` für den Message-Append — zwei parallele Ingest-Aufrufe für dieselbe `providerMessageId` (Watch-Push vs. Poll-Reconciliation-Überschneidung) liefern jetzt beide `{ duplicate: scheitert (#1038, Finding aus PR-Review #952). - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework@0.150.0 - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-headless@0.150.0 - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer@0.150.0 - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dispatcher-live@0.150.0 - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-web@0.150.0
